elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." followed by the retained sentence "The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." No residual unlimited-Customer-liability language remains.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 21.1 as rendered: "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000." The edit deliberately uses lower-case "fees" scoped to the Agreement and all Order Forms, so the illusory §1.5 "Fees" = USD 12,000 Implementation Fee definition and the "first Order Form" confinement no longer drive the cap; basis (paid or payable, not "all amounts"), temporal anchor (preceding the claim) and the USD 1,000,000 floor all match literally.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.2 (retained): "Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill..." — bilateral by its terms; the Customer-favourable direct-damages sentence is preserved.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 defines Excluded Claims to include "a Party's breach of confidentiality... obligations", and 21.1/21.2 both open "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations" sits inside Excluded Claims, which are outside the 21.1 cap.
21.3: "its indemnification obligations" listed as an Excluded Claim; the cap in 21.1 is expressly "Except for Excluded Claims".
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" within Excluded Claims.
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" within Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" within Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: 21.3 as rendered: "Customer's payment obligations, including undisputed amounts due for conforming Services, are not damages and are not limited by this Section." The carve-out now runs to payment obligations as a whole rather than the narrow §1.5 "Fees" subset, while the Customer-favourable "undisputed"/"conforming Services" language survives as an illustrative inclusion.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1 "each Party's total aggregate liability" plus "The cap is mutual".

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: 21.1: "fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim", no longer tied to the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee definition.
21.3 Excluded Claims includes "its indemnification obligations"; 21.1 cap applies "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "breach of confidentiality... obligations".

reasons: Deviation call is correct: as drafted the cap was pegged to "Fees" = the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, i.e. far below six months' fees and squarely in walk-away territory, and the §21.3 payment carve-out inherited the same illusory defined term.

Every preferred element is met in operative language: the cap is expressly mutual, the basis is now the greater of fees paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, the indirect/consequential exclusion is bilateral, and the Excluded Claims list already carries all seven required uncapped categories.

The payment carve-out is repaired at the right level of generality: it now reaches "Customer's payment obligations" as a whole rather than the narrowly defined subset of Fees, satisfying the definition-resolution requirement for Customer-payment carve-outs.

Minimality holds. Only the two defective phrases were touched (cap basis in 21.1 and the Fees-limited payment sentence in 21.3). The drafter avoided the cleaner-looking but broader route of rewriting §1.5/§1.6 by using lower-case "fees" scoped to the Agreement and all Order Forms; "and all Order Forms" is necessary rather than surplus because the original expressly confined the cap to the first Order Form. No survival tails, procedures, expense language or extra damages categories were added, and no explanatory examples were bolted onto the formula.

Intent is preserved: the mutual "regardless of the form of action or number of claims" sentence, the Customer-favourable direct-damages sentence in 21.2 (data restoration, replacement services, notices, incident response), and the "undisputed"/"conforming Services" qualifier all survive without contradiction; the retained §1.5/§1.6 definitions still function elsewhere and leave no dangling cross-reference or undefined term.

Optional polish only, not a defect: the coexistence of defined "Fees" (Implementation Fee only) and lower-case "fees" in 21.1 could be made airtight with a short parenthetical such as "(regardless of the definition of 'Fees' in Section 1.5)", but the current self-describing formulation is unambiguous and adding it would risk non-minimality.
